title: Financial literacy: banking, budgets, interest and credit
purpose: Make and follow a budget, compare checking and savings accounts, calculate simple and compound interest, understand paychecks and taxes, use debit and credit cards safely, read a credit card statement, see how borrowing costs add up, and avoid scams.
primary_reading: Next Gen Personal Finance: free middle-school curriculum

weeks.3: Banks and credit unions: checking and savings
weeks.5: Compound interest and the rule of 72
weeks.6: Saving and investing: why starting early matters
weeks.7: Paychecks: gross pay, taxes and net pay
weeks.8: Spending: comparison shopping and unit prices
weeks.9: Debit cards, credit cards and credit scores
weeks.10: The cost of borrowing: loans and minimum payments
weeks.11: Protecting your money: scams, fraud and identity theft
weeks.12: Planning for the future: jobs, education and goals

blocks.deliverable: Make a monthly budget for a given allowance or paycheck.
Compare two savings accounts by the interest they pay.
Calculate a savings balance after 1, 5 and 10 years.
Week 7 midterm; read a sample pay stub and find net pay.
Show how long a card balance takes to pay off at the minimum.
Write a one-page plan for a goal five years away.
Submit the project; take an unseen 45 minute final in week 14.

project: My money plan: design a one-year plan for a realistic teen budget with income, spending categories and a savings goal; compare two savings accounts and one credit option using interest calculations; and explain three choices you would make and why.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
